lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: follow a tray line, choose set courses, pay first, and find a seat
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: At a workers' canteen, follow the line, choose a first and second course, and pay at the register before sitting.
lessons.title: Following the workplace lunch line
lessons.objective: Follow a workplace canteen tray line, choose two courses, ask about advance payment, and find an open seat.
lessons.focus: 列はどこからですか asks where the queue starts; 列の最後 means its end, where a new arrival joins. レジで先に払いますか asks whether payment comes first. 主菜 means main course. 席は空いていますか asks whether a seat is free.
lessons.scene: Sam eats at a workplace canteen with a tray service line.

cards.ja: 定食には何が付きますか
cards.en: What comes with the set meal?

cards.ja: 最初の料理はスープをお願いします
cards.en: Soup for the first course, please

cards.ja: レジで先に払いますか
cards.en: Do we pay first at the register?

cards.ja: この席は空いていますか

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。列はどこからですか。
reader.en: Excuse me. Where does the line start?

reader.speaker: Worker
reader.ja: あちらからです。トレーを取ってください。
reader.en: Over there. Please take a tray.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 日替わり定食には何が付きますか。
reader.en: What comes with the daily set meal?

reader.speaker: Worker
reader.ja: スープと主菜と飲み物が付きます。
reader.en: It includes soup, a main course, and a drink.

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: 最初の料理は何にしますか。
reader.en: What would you like for the first course?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: スープをお願いします。主菜は鶏の煮込みでお願いします。
reader.en: Soup, please. For the main course, the chicken stew.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: レジで先に払いますか。
reader.en: Do we pay first at the register?

reader.speaker: Worker
reader.ja: はい、席に着く前にお願いします。
reader.en: Yes, before taking a seat, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 分かりました。この席は空いていますか。
reader.en: Understood. Is this seat free?

reader.speaker: Worker
reader.ja: はい、空いています。
reader.en: Yes, it is.

speaking.opening: トレーを取って、列にお並びください。
speaking.goal: Find the start of the line, ask what comes with the set meal, choose soup and a main dish, ask whether to pay first, and check an open seat.
speaking.closure: この席は空いていますか。

lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: ask about children's portions, plain dishes, high chairs, and sharing an adult plate
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Your picky six-year-old will only eat plain pasta; ask the kitchen what they can prepare and how it will be priced.
lessons.title: Lunch with a child and a baby
lessons.objective: Ask for a high chair, a small plain pasta portion for a child, its price, and an extra plate to share an adult meal.
lessons.focus: 子ども用 means for children. ソースなし means without sauce; バターを少し means a little butter. 取り皿 is an extra small plate for sharing. 〜を作れますか asks whether the kitchen can prepare it.
lessons.scene: Ana brings her six-year-old child and baby to a lunch restaurant.

cards.ja: ベビーチェアはありますか
cards.en: Do you have a high chair?

cards.ja: 子ども用の量はありますか
ソースなしのパスタを作れますか
cards.en: Can you make plain pasta without sauce?

cards.ja: バターを少しだけお願いします
小さめのパスタはいくらですか
cards.en: How much is the small pasta portion?

cards.ja: 取り皿を一枚お願いします
cards.en: One extra plate for sharing, please

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 赤ちゃん用のベビーチェアはありますか。
reader.en: Do you have a high chair for the baby?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、あります。
reader.en: Yes, we do.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 子ども用の量はありますか。
reader.en: Do you have child-size portions?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 小さめのパスタを作れます。
reader.en: We can make a smaller pasta portion.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 六歳の子はソースなしのパスタを食べます。
reader.en: My six-year-old eats pasta without sauce.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: バターを少しだけお願いします。
reader.en: Just a little butter, please.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 小さめのパスタはいくらですか。
reader.en: How much is the small pasta portion?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 六百円です。
reader.en: It is 600 yen.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 赤ちゃんと私の料理を分けます。取り皿を一枚お願いします。
reader.en: I will share my meal with the baby. One extra plate, please.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: かしこまりました。
reader.en: Certainly.

speaking.opening: お子様は何名様ですか。
speaking.goal: Ask for a high chair, child-size plain pasta without sauce with a little butter, its price, and an extra plate to share.
speaking.closure: 取り皿を一枚お願いします。

lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: ask about step-free entry, restrooms, quiet tables, and space for mobility aids
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Call a lunch spot to ask whether it has step-free access and a table that fits a wheelchair.
lessons.title: Calling ahead about access
lessons.objective: Ask by phone about step-free entry, ramp location, wheelchair-usable restroom, walker space, and a quiet table before reserving.
lessons.focus: 段差なく入れますか asks whether one can enter without steps. 車いすで使えるトイレ asks whether the restroom can be used with a wheelchair. 歩行器 means walker. 〜のスペースはありますか asks whether space is available.
lessons.scene: Ana phones a restaurant before bringing her parents to lunch.

cards.ja: スロープはどこですか
車いすで使えるトイレはありますか
席に車いすのスペースはありますか
cards.en: Is there room for a wheelchair at the table?

cards.ja: 静かな席はありますか
父は車いすを使います
母は歩行器を使います
四人で一時に予約したいです
cards.en: I would like to reserve for four at one o’clock

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: こんにちは。入口から段差なく入れますか。
reader.en: Hello. Can we enter without steps?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、スロープがあります。
reader.en: Yes, there is a ramp.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: スロープはどこですか。
reader.en: Where is the ramp?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 正面玄関の右側です。
reader.en: To the right of the main entrance.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 車いすで使えるトイレはありますか。
reader.en: Is there a wheelchair-usable restroom?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、あります。
reader.en: Yes, there is.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 父は車いすを使います。母は歩行器を使います。
reader.en: My father uses a wheelchair. My mother uses a walker.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 席に車いすのスペースはありますか。静かな席もありますか。
reader.en: Is there room for a wheelchair at the table? Is there a quiet table too?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい。窓の近くに静かな席をご用意できます。
reader.en: Yes. We can prepare a quiet table near the window.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: では、四人で一時に予約したいです。
reader.en: Then I would like to reserve for four at one o’clock.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 承知しました。
reader.en: Understood.

speaking.opening: お電話ありがとうございます。
speaking.goal: Ask about step-free entry, ramp location, restroom use with a wheelchair, room for a walker and wheelchair, and a quiet table; reserve for four.
speaking.closure: 四人で一時に予約したいです。
